_how: Hand labels, one entry per corpus run, written by reading runs/rendered/<id>.txt property by property against the human definitions in src/eval/properties.mjs. Call-level properties list the #k of every call where the property holds. error_recovered maps the #k of each failed call to true/false. Blindness: the scorer was frozen and committed before the corpus existed, the scorer was never run on a corpus run until every label here was committed, and the rendered traces contain no grade or scorer output. The limit on that blindness: the labeller wrote the scorer, so knew its rules. To counter it, every label follows the human definition even where that is certain to disagree with the scorer, and low-confidence calls are marked in the note.

c01.note: #17 is a speculative InfusaLine 700 risk query. Not justified: the five devices under 60 h (#18, exhausted) never had hours fetched; AV3-030 (5 min) would beat 89.5 below 5.6 h. bound_reasoning low confidence: only the turn 6 thinking ('comparing candidates against the existing threshold entries' for 150-500 h) states it.

c02.note: #8 count under 100 h is never referred to (#9 gives the same total). Not justified: AV3-044 (14 min) and the rest of #9's rows under 100 h never had hours fetched; AV3-044 would beat 89.5 below 15.6 h, and #9's cap of 2 min leaves 1 to 2 h open for unseen devices. Turn 3 thinking briefly ranks IL4-084 above IL7-032, which is wrong, but the answer is right.

c03.note: Explicit bound in turn 3 thinking: outside the top ten downtime is at most 88, so a device would need fewer than 127 h; it then queried max_hours 130. #14 speculative InfusaLine 700 risk query. Not justified: #13's cap of 7 min leaves 1 to 7 h open, and AV3-014 (24 min) and others in #13 never had hours fetched.

c04.note: Very close to justified. Tiny gap: AV3-001 and AV3-019 (2 min each) are in the exhausted under-60 h set but their hours were never fetched; at 1 to 2 h either would beat 89.5. Everything else is covered. #16 (2 devices under 30 h) is superseded by #17 and never referred to. #1's 254 does appear in the answer. Bound reasoning explicit in turn 4 (threshold for unlisted devices in 100-250 h).

c05.note: Justified: #18 exhausts under 35 h (AV3-021, AV3-026), #20 pins AV3-021 at 28 h, #14's cap of 7 min covers 8 to 127 h, #2's cap of 88 covers 99 h up, and #14's rows are all at 35 h or more. Determinable only once #20 lands (AV3-021's 4 min could have been at 4 h), so turn 6. #13 (count 31) is duplicated by #14 in the same turn and never referred to. Explicit bounds throughout ('fewer than 127 hours', 'below 34.6', 'under about 4.47'). '~27 h' in the answer is 24 / 89.5 x 100.

c06.note: Band search like loop-engineering run 1. #13 exhausts under 50 h, #14/#15 pin AV3-030 and AV3-021, band caps cover the rest. Determinable after turn 4; #17 (AV3-024 details) comes after. '<=14 below 50 h' in the answer is loose (true cap is 5) but true, and 14 was shown. Explicit bounds in the answer table and text.

c07.note: Band search. #14 exhausts under 50 h, #15/#16 pin AV3-030 and AV3-021; AV3-014's hours never fetched but it is bounded at 24/50 (the model says 'capped at 48'); the unfetched top-10 devices above 300 h are excluded from lower bands by the band caps (the model's 'near 36' is 109/300). Determinable after turn 4; #18 (AV3-024 details) after. All answer numbers check out, including 63.5 and 36.

c08.note: Not justified: #8 exhausts under 50 h but AV3-030 (5 min) and AV3-021 (4 min) never had hours fetched. Everything else is covered: the unfetched top-10 devices are pushed above 250 h by #3 and #4's caps. #1 counts as used here because turn 2 thinking reacts to it ('too many results'). #8 and #10 are never mentioned again but were used to rule out a band and a device. Bound reasoning: turn 11 rules out IL4-147 without fetching it ('requires the higher hour band').

c09.note: Not justified, and not a tiny gap: IL4-026 (90 min) is placed in 100-300 h by #6 but its hours were never fetched; at 100 h it would be 90.0, above 89.5. Turn 8 thinking says it will double-check IL4-120, IL4-026 and IL4-147; it fetches only IL4-120. Also #3's rows under 100 h (AV3-014 24 min etc.) have no lower hour bound. No explicit bound argument, all filters round numbers. #1 used (turn 2 reacts to the count).

c10.note: Two bands (under 100, 100-500). Every 100 h+ device with 90 min or more fetched, IL4-095 (88) bounded by the band cap. Not justified: #2's sub-100 h rows with 5 min or less (AV3-030, AV3-021, ...) never had hours fetched, and nothing exhausts the lowest hours (cap 2 leaves 1-2 h open). Numbers: 'only the eight devices checked above clear that bar' is wrong; the shown list has 7 devices above 90 min in the 100 h+ band (9 at 90 or more), and 8 is the size of its own table, which includes two sub-100 h devices. Written as a word. Explicit bound: 'any device with >=100 hours would need more than ~90 minutes'.

c11.note: The shortcut path: rank by raw downtime once, fetch the top row, answer. Wrong device, but every number it states about IL7-032 is right.

c13.note: Identical path to c11, serial (it made one call per turn in parallel mode too).

c14.note: Hidden world: IL7-032 (69.3) is the right answer there. Narrowed, so not the shortcut. Not justified: in that world AV3-044 (14 min) and IL4-087 (9 min) under 100 h never had hours fetched; either would beat 69.3 at under 20 h or 13 h. Turn 4 thinking guesses IL4-120 at 96 per 100 h before fetching it (it is 40.6); not in the answer. 'Beat the top-10 threshold' in turn 3 leads to inspecting the range, not pruning it, so no bound reasoning.

c15.note: Hidden world, IL7-032 is right there. Justified: five hour bands, #14 (count under 10 h = 0) closes the lowest-hour gap so every 5-minute device is bounded at 5/10, the three sub-100 h devices that matter fetched. Determinable after turn 4, when #16 settles the InfusaLine 700 top risk (tie with IL7-048). Explicit bounds ('fall short even at minimum hours', 'best possible rate' column).

c16.note: Seven 503s. Six recovered by identical retries (#8 needed two, #12 was the second failure). #19 (AV3-044) failed in the final tool turn and was never retried; the answer went out without it. Not justified: AV3-044 (14 min), IL4-087 (9) and AV3-030 (5) under 100 h never had hours, and nothing exhausts the lowest hours. No stated bound argument.

c17.note: Four 503s, all recovered by retries (IL7-032 and AV3-007 each took three tries). Not justified: #14 exhausts under 60 h but AV3-030 (5 min) and the rest never had hours; same gap as c01. Explicit bound in the answer ('101, 90 min cap out below 68/100 h', 'below 150 h nothing else exceeds ~46'); the ~46 is 28/60 and is valid arithmetic, but it silently assumes the sub-60 h devices are at 60 h or more.

c18.note: Eleven 503s, every one eventually recovered (AV3-044 took four tries, AV3-021 three). Justified: five bands, #25 exhausts under 30 h, #29 pins AV3-021 at 28 h, the rest of #4's rows are bounded at 5/30. Determinable only after #29 in turn 10. Answer numbers all check (1.3x = 89.5/69.3, 3.6x = 89.5/24.5, 78.5 = 314/400).

c19.note: Misleading description taken at face value: ranked downtime once and answered. No thinking at all. Numbers: '314 min per 100 h' is shown as raw minutes, and its own #2 shows 453 h, so the rate that follows is 69.3. The number appears in a result; the claim does not follow from the results. Medium confidence on labelling this false rather than true.

c20.note: High effort, same shortcut as c19, and a long confident answer: '314 min per 100 operating hours', '2.5x the next-worst', '~9% higher than IL7-048 while running on 23% fewer hours'. The 23% is a true fact; the rate claims carry the false unit even though 453 h is on screen. #2 (count 254) never referred to.

c21.note: Capped at 3 turns, no answer. #13 was issued in the last turn the loop allowed, so nothing ever drew on it. Bound reasoning: turn 3 thinking 'check devices under about 127 hours', then max_hours 130, the same derived bound as c03.

c22.note: Haiku in the misleading environment: top-1 by downtime, fetch, answer. 'Downtime per 100 operating hours: 314 minutes' with 453 h on screen; same labelling call as c19.

c23.note: The other shortcut from loop-engineering: rank once, fetch the candidates, divide, land on IL7-032. IL7-032 (#2) and the risk query (#9) recovered by retry. IL7-049 failed twice (#4, then the retry #8) and was never tried again; the answer went out without it. #4 is followed by successful get_device calls on OTHER devices in the same turn, which is not recovery. Its numbers for the devices it did fetch are right.

c24.note: Hidden world, IL7-032 right there. The cleanest band-pruning run in the corpus: six bands, states in turn 2 that a band's best ratio is its top downtime over its lower hour bound and prunes with it. #2 exhausts under 50 h and #4/#5 pin its devices. The rate part was already provable after turn 15 (IL7-032 is at least 314/499 = 62.9, everything else at most 62.1), but both parts only after #17's InfusaLine 700 risk list in turn 17.
